simple_description: A type of migraine preceded or accompanied by temporary sensory disturbances, most commonly visual changes like flashing lights, zigzag patterns, or blind spots, followed by throbbing head pain.
medical_description: Recurrent attacks of fully reversible neurological symptoms (aura) that usually develop gradually over 5-20 minutes and last fewer than 60 minutes, caused by cortical spreading depression, followed within 60 minutes by a migraine headache.
affected_system: Cerebral cortex (occipital and parietal lobes) and trigeminovascular pathways.
symptoms: Visual aura (90% of cases): scintillating scotoma, shimmering zigzag lines (fortification spectra), blind spots
Sensory aura: unilateral numbness or tingling pins-and-needles creeping up hand and face
Speech/language aura: transient word-finding difficulty or mild dysphasia
Followed by unilateral or bilateral pulsating headache, nausea, and photophobia
early_warning_signs: Gradual onset of shimmering visual disturbances expanding across the visual field over 15 to 30 minutes
possible_causes: Cortical spreading depression (CSD): a self-propagating wave of cellular depolarization across cerebral cortical neurons and glia
Subsequent neurogenic inflammation and trigeminal sensitization
risk_factors: Female sex and fluctuating estrogen levels
Use of combined oral contraceptive pills (contraindicated in migraine with aura due to ischemic stroke risk)
disease_types: Migraine with typical aura (visual, sensory, or speech)
clinical_evaluation: Careful neurological history confirming gradual spread (> 5 min) and resolution (< 60 min) of symptoms to distinguish from acute ischemic stroke / TIA (which have abrupt sudden onset).
diagnostic_tests: Brain MRI with DWI (Diffusion-Weighted Imaging) - Essential on first presentation to definitively rule out acute ischemic stroke or intracranial lesion
MRA or CTA of head and neck if vascular malformation suspected
treatment_overview: Abortive triptans should be taken at the onset of the *headache* phase (not during the aura phase). Preventive therapy with beta-blockers, lamotrigine (effective specifically for aura), or CGRP inhibitors.
medication_classes: Acute headache phase: Triptans, NSAIDs, Gepants
Aura-specific prevention: Lamotrigine, Topiramate, Flunarizine, Magnesium
precautions: Absolute contraindication for estrogen-containing contraceptives or HRT due to heightened thrombotic stroke risk
prevention: Consistent daily sleep patterns, hydration, and avoidance of flickering strobe lights or screen glare
complications: Migrainous infarction (ischemic stroke developing in territory of aura)
emergency_signs: Aura symptoms that start suddenly within seconds (rather than gradual minutes)
Weakness or paralysis of one side of the body (motor symptoms)
Aura lasting longer than 60 minutes without returning to baseline

faqs.question: Can I have aura without a headache?
faqs.answer: Yes. This is termed 'Typical aura without headache' (formerly acephalgic migraine), where visual flashing or sensory tingling occurs for 20-30 minutes without subsequent head pain.

faqs.question: Why is estrogen contraindicated?
faqs.answer: Because migraine with aura slightly increases baseline risk of ischemic stroke, and estrogen-containing oral contraceptives multiply this thrombotic risk significantly.

hi.name: माइग्रेन विथ ऑरा (Migraine with aura)
hi.summary: सिरदर्द से ठीक पहले आंखों के सामने चमक, ज़िगज़ैग रेखाएं या हाथ में झनझनाहट महसूस होना, जिसके बाद तेज धड़कने वाला सिरदर्द होता है।
hi.advice: जब ऑरा दिखे तो तुरंत वाहन चलाना या स्क्रीन देखना बंद करें और शांत अंधेरे कमरे में लेट जाएं।

hinglish.name: Migraine with Aura (Visual flashes ke sath sar dard)
hinglish.summary: Sar dard shuru hone se 20-30 min pehle aakho ke aage chamkile dhabbe ya zigzag line dikhna fir tez dard hona.
hinglish.advice: Screen se door rahein aur doctor se prescription lein.

ur.summary: سر درد سے پہلے آنکھوں کے سامنے چمکدار لکیریں یا اندھا پن ظاہر ہونا اور پھر شدید درد کا آغاز۔
ur.advice: علامات شروع ہوتے ہی پرسکون ماحول میں آرام کریں۔
